assertions.source: kappa(3)/kappa(41) recomputed from the mirror-series witness matches the 2.098835 recorded in em-linking-fh-link-bound-correction.witness.json. Reproducing the figures I dispute, before disputing them: the dispute is about which observable the bound applies to, not about arithmetic.

assertions.name: kappa_divides_out_the_pair_count
assertions.source: split/(n_pairs*kappa) is constant to 5.0e-8 across all 31 rows, and n_pairs == Z-1 exactly on every row (True). So kappa is definitionally a per-pair ratio with the pp-pair count divided out -- not an energy for eq. (43), which bounds one, to be confronted with.

assertions.name: mirror_split_grows_13x_where_constant_charge_flux_predicts_exactly_1
assertions.source: THE RESULT. Under a vertex-transitive carrier with charge-only flux and eq. (43) saturated, dE = C*a*m*(Z-N)(Phi_p-Phi_n) is A-INDEPENDENT for the d=1 ladder -- this ratio would be exactly 1. It is 13.63. So constant fluxes are refuted and the required Phi_p-Phi_n must GROW by that factor. Pinned to the measured value so the refutation cannot silently regress.

assertions.name: required_flux_growth_is_opposite_in_sign_to_the_recorded_decline
assertions.source: The corpus records the obligation as a flux DECLINE of 1.449. Confronting the bound with the energy rather than the per-pair ratio makes it a flux-difference GROWTH of 13.63 -- opposite in sign, 9.4x in magnitude. Both directions positive: True.

description: EXPLORATORY. The Freedman-He link bound (Komendarczyk eq. 43) has a charge-blind right-hand side -- only link topology and fluxes -- while kappa(A) is built from a mirror-pair split, which is pure charge. So the open obligation is not Flux(A) but the pair (Flux_p, Flux_n). Under a vertex-transitive carrier with charge-only flux, the d=1 mirror split is C*a*m*(Phi_p - Phi_n) -- ONE CONSTANT for the whole A=3..63 ladder. The data grows by 13.63, so constant fluxes are refuted and the required Phi-difference must GROW by 13.63. The corpus records the obligation as a DECLINE by 1.449, which is sqrt(kappa(3)/kappa(41)) read off kappa -- but kappa is split/((Z-1)*u), a per-pair ratio with the pair count already divided out, not an energy. Both figures are reproduced here. Scope-(a) on the model class {vertex-transitive carrier} x {charge-only flux} x {saturation}; eq. (43) itself is untouched. Nothing wired.

eq43_source.charge_blind: every factor on the right is link topology (ac) or flux; nothing in it distinguishes a proton from a neutron, so charge can only enter via Flux
eq43_source.it_is_a_LOWER_BOUND: using (43) as an equality assumes saturation. Nothing in this corpus establishes it; the assumption is recorded, not discharged

kappa_is_a_per_pair_ratio_not_an_energy.why_it_matters: the pp-pair count (Z-1) is already divided out of kappa, so confronting eq. (43) -- a bound on an ENERGY -- with kappa asks it to explain a per-pair ratio. The energy-like observable is the split.

what_would_have_to_be_supplied.not_one_function: the obligation is the PAIR (Phi_p, Phi_n), not a single Flux(A); a charge-blind bound cannot produce a charge-driven observable otherwise
what_would_have_to_be_supplied.and_the_framework_defines_no_flux: `Flux` occurs nowhere in folio/quantum-observable-universe/lean/ as a quantity. The grep hits are a photon docstring (KnotRegistry.lean:48), meson colour flux tubes (MesonFluxTubeReduction.lean), and the English idiom "in flux in Mathlib's CoxeterSystem API" (Tw.lean:56, Defn.lean:114, Quotient.lean:62,136). Measured, not recalled.
what_would_have_to_be_supplied.escape_hatches_not_excluded: a carrier that is NOT vertex-transitive, or an ac that depends on the charge assignment, or an unsaturated bound, all evade this. Each is a further thing to derive, not a thing the sources supply.
